subject: Clarification: outputs, retraining consent & feedback license for Services Agreement
messages:
From: Amelia Cruz <amelia.cruz@atlashealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify rights for outputs and retraining — draft Services Agreement attached

Hi Michael,

Thanks for the draft Services Agreement and SOW. Procurement and legal ran a quick review and flagged a few items we need clarified before we can proceed to procurement sign-off:

1) Output ownership: current draft is ambiguous about whether Atlas owns the model outputs (generated text, summaries, derivatives) or whether Redwood reserves rights to aggregate or commercialize outputs. We need explicit customer ownership of outputs produced from Atlas data for the time period of the contract.

2) Model retraining and use of Atlas data: the redline references a feedback license, but is broad. Atlas cannot consent to any training/retraining without an opt-in, narrow purpose, and strict de-identification.

3) Feedback telemetry / telemetry retention: can Redwood provide a retention window and confirm what fields are collected? (We prefer event-level telemetry retention no longer than 90 days unless otherwise agreed.)

4) Derivative/attribution: we want to ensure Atlas cannot be attributed as a data source for public model training or marketing.

Attached is a marked-up version with in-line comments (Atlas_Services_Agg_v3_redline.docx). Can you confirm Redwood's standard positions and whether you can accept language that: (a) gives Atlas ownership of outputs; (b) limits Redwood to a non-exclusive, anonymized feedback license used only to improve hosted service quality and not to train external models; and (c) permits an explicit customer opt-out for retraining?

We are hoping to close legal review by 2027-04-26 to meet procurement timelines. If helpful, we can get legal on a quick call.

Thanks,
Amelia Cruz
Sr. Contracts Manager | Atlas Health
Attachment: Atlas_Services_Agg_v3_redline.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amelia Cruz <amelia.cruz@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify rights for outputs and retraining — draft Services Agreement attached

Hi Amelia — thanks for the markups and the timeline. Appreciate the specificity; that helps.

Quick summary of our plan from Redwood:
- We generally expect customers to retain ownership of their outputs; our standard Order Form/Exhibit language grants customers broad usage rights.
- On training/retraining: our default hosted terms historically include a limited feedback license to improve and operate the service, but customers can opt out of model-training usage via order-form toggles or an explicit opt-out clause. We need to confirm the exact redline text that enforces opt-out and the consequences for product support/SLOs.
- Telemetry: we can provide an export of fields we collect and propose a 90-day retention window for usage events; logs required for security/SLA investigations may be retained longer under exception provisions.

Putting Karthik and Laura on thread to coordinate proposed redline language. Vanessa, would appreciate if you can pull the telemetry field list we keep for hosted customers and an internal note on how opt-out affects performance diagnostics.

I can do a 30–45 min call tomorrow (2027-04-19) to walk through Atlas' redlines if that helps.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: MG-proposed-language.txt (text/plain)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: internal — proposed positions on Atlas redlines

Internal notes / suggested positions for reply to Atlas (high level, with language stubs):

1) Outputs: position: customer owns outputs. Proposed clause: "Customer Ownership of Outputs: Customer shall retain all right, title and interest in and to Outputs (defined as model-generated content produced for Customer). Redwood hereby assigns to Customer all rights necessary for Customer's internal and commercial use of Outputs, subject to the limited feedback license below."

2) Feedback license: position: limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, purpose-limited to service improvement and operations, with de-identification. Proposed clause: "Feedback License: Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use de-identified Feedback (aggregate or de-identified usage data) to operate and improve Redwood's services. Redwood shall not use Customer Data or Outputs to train models for sale to third parties without Customer's prior written consent."

3) Model retraining / opt-out: position: Customer may opt-out of training/retraining. If opt-out is exercised, Redwood will provide reasonable alternative support but may exclude Customer from certain model-improvement releases. Proposed clause: "Training Opt-Out: Customer may elect in the Order Form to exclude Customer Data and Outputs from model training and persistent model updates. Redwood's obligations under the Service Levels shall remain, except to the extent performance degradation is directly attributable to opt-out status."

4) Telemetry & retention: position: disclose fields + default 90-day retention for event telemetry; security incident logs may be retained up to 2 years for investigation.

5) Attribution / marketing: position: no attribution of Customer as a data source. Add explicit non-attribution language.

6) Escrow / evidence: for high-risk regulated customers, offer contract language for a limited training escrow (time-limited, scope-limited) and a review mechanism.

Thoughts on the negotiation strategy: take Outputs and Opt-Out as baseline concessions; push for explicit de-identification and a narrow feedback license. If Atlas demands absolute prohibition on any derivative use, escalate to legal for potential crediting/price adjustment.

I can draft track-changes for the specific paragraphs and send to Amelia by EOD.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial | Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amelia Cruz <amelia.cruz@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Ben Monroe <ben.monroe@atlashealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed language for Outputs / Training / Feedback (see inline)

Hi Amelia — following up with proposed text (inline for ease):

--- proposed language start ---
1) Customer Ownership of Outputs: Customer shall retain all right, title and interest in and to Outputs (defined as model-generated content produced for Customer under this Agreement).

2) Feedback License: Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use de-identified and aggregated Feedback solely to operate and improve the Redwood-hosted service provided to Customer. Feedback will not be used to train or improve models that are sold or otherwise made available to third parties without Customer's prior written consent.

3) Training Opt-Out: Customer may elect, by checkbox on the Order Form or written notice, to exclude Customer Data and Outputs from Redwood's model training processes. If Customer elects Opt-Out, Redwood may be unable to incorporate Customer-specific improvements into future model versions provided to Customer and may, at Redwood's discretion, adjust service availability for certain premium features.

4) Telemetry & Retention: Redwood will provide a data inventory of telemetry fields collected and will retain non-PI telemetry by default for 90 days. Logs necessary for security incident investigation may be retained for up to 730 days and will be stored and accessed only by authorized personnel.
--- proposed language end ---

Can you please confirm whether the language above addresses Atlas' concerns or propose edits inline? If acceptable, we can prepare a clean Order Form and DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Michael
Attachment: proposed-language.txt (text/plain)

From: Ben Monroe <ben.monroe@atlashealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Amelia Cruz <amelia.cruz@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed language for Outputs / Training / Feedback (see inline)

Michael / team — thanks for the proposed text and for the opt-out option; that goes a long way. A few minor edits from Atlas legal to finalize:

• In the second sentence of the Feedback License clause, replace "de-identified and aggregated" with "de-identified, aggregated, and subject to our independent re-identification assessment" and add that re-identification risk assessments will be mutually agreed on an annual basis.

• In Training Opt-Out, add a sentence that any use of Customer Data for internal benchmarking (not model training) will be aggregated and not re-identifiable.

• Finally, we need an explicit non-attribution clause: "Redwood will not attribute Customer, Customer Data, or Outputs as a source for any public model or marketing materials without Customer's prior written consent."

If you can accept these edits, we are ready to proceed to DocuSign. I've attached a short annotated acceptance and will route to procurement once accepted (DocuSign-Envelope-78910.link).

Best regards,
Ben Monroe
Senior Counsel | Atlas Health
Attachment: DocuSign-Envelope-78910.link
